title: Microprobe Orchestrator: Prefill-aware Execution Policy and Attention Fallback
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Our runtime currently relies on static kernel routing rules that underperform for mixed workloads (variable seq-len and heterogenous GPU fleet). At high concurrency the wrong attention implementation or prefill/decode scheduling policy can increase p50/p95 latency and reduce GPU utilization. Goal: Implement a microprobe-driven orchestrator that probes a small subset of requests to build a live fingerprint (arch x seq-len x batch) and uses lightweight heuristics + online autotuning to pick kernels and attention paths with low regret. Must be prefill-aware (selecting different kernels or batching strategies for long prefill vs short chat turns) and support graceful fallback to safe generic implementations under uncertainty.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Orchestrator can classify incoming requests into fingerprint buckets (gpu_arch, seq_len_bucket, batch_size) with <5% classification overhead.
2) For target seq-len distributions (16/64/512) on test harness, p95 latency reduction >=10% and throughput uplift >=8% compared to static baseline.
3) Online probe budget is configurable and defaults to 2% of requests; probe rollback logic avoids sustained regressions (no more than 1% requests with >20% increased latency compared to baseline).
4) System logs chosen kernel and probe outcome; rollout can be disabled per-customer and per-region.
5) Unit/integration tests + performance harness + PR ready for review.
proposed_solution:
Phase 1: lightweight profiler hooks in prefill path that record seq-len, batch size, and GPU flavor (CUDA compute capability / memory). Implement microprobe manager that marks a small percentage of requests to run in experimental kernel variants (attention implementation A/B, cuBLAS vs custom kernel, different blocking). Collect metrics (latency, GPU SM utilization, memory pressure) and store short-term aggregates in an in-memory fingerprint table.
Phase 2: heuristic policy engine that maps fingerprints to preferred kernels using rules derived from offline benchmarking (e.g., seqlen<64 -> fused attention kernel X, seqlen>256 on Ampere -> chunked attention Y). Policies encoded as ranked preferences with confidence scores.
Phase 3: online autotuner that updates preferences when probe evidence shows regret > configured threshold; includes rollback (exponential backoff) and safety net to avoid oscillation. Expose config via runtime flags and Console surface (per-model).
Phase 4: integrate prefill-aware scheduling: detect long prefill windows and adjust batching window, KV cache reuse, and attention chunking strategy to lower decode latency for subsequent short turns.
Instrumentation: trace rules, probe IDs, chosen kernel variant, rollback events, and customer opt-out.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature branch + unit tests (1 week).
2) Internal canary on dev cluster with synthetic workload (seq-len sweep) to validate metrics pipeline (2 weeks).
3) Small beta: opt-in for internal Redwood services and 2 customers (~2% traffic) to validate in mixed production (2 weeks).
4) Gradual rollout by customer cohort with monitoring dashboards and automatic disable if SLO regressions detected (staged over 4 weeks).
5) Post-rollout: run 2-week evaluation, update heuristic table from observed fingerprints, refine probe budget defaults.
Ops: rollback button in Console and kill-switch via config flag.
